comments.text:
Horse piss....I started working in construction in 1976... in the field while in college. In 1980, I took a job as an estimator. At that time, EVERY yard of concrete that was poured, steel that was set, framing, sheetrock, painting, and roofing was ALL done by White, Black, and Native American citizens, with a few Hispanic Americans as well. They all made a living wage, owned a home, and sent their kids (like me) to college. We had crews that had grandfathers, fathers, and sons all working together and passing down knowledge, craftsmanship, and skills.

From 1976 until the mid-1980s, I came across one immigrant plasterer who came here legally from England. I had never even heard anyone speaking Spanish outside of my Spanish class until the mid-1980s, when they started showing up by the carload fresh from south of the border. They worked hard, but they also worked VERY cheaply, and contractors—from the GC level all the way through the trades—took advantage.

Wages stagnated as they used these immigrants to drive down costs, cut benefits, and drive up profits. That drove out the Americans, and all that craftsmanship and skill went with them. This is not an ICE problem; this was a combination of cowards in Congress failing to do their job... and greedy contractors who wanted to pad the profit sharing at the expense of the American workers WHO WERE BUILDING THIS COUNTRY... EVERY DAMN BIT OF IT.
